item.title: Meet young professionals in European Standardization: Markus Beckman from Sweden
item.description: Young professionals bring new energy, ideas, and skills to European standardization. As our society undergoes rapid transformations, their contributions are key to ensuring that standards remain relevant, forward-looking, and impactful. In the context of the green and digital transitions, and as Europe strengthens its efforts to build a skilled and future-oriented workforce, we are continuing our interview series dedicated to young professionals. Through conversations with young professionals working in standardization across different sectors and countries, we highlight their experiences, motivations, and visions for the future. item.title: Get to know the nominees for the 2026 Standards+Innovations awards
item.description: It is again time to celebrate the contribution of research to standardization as well as the important contributions to bring standardization into the classrooms. At the closure of the call for nominations, total of 26 submissions has been made by CEN and CENELEC members in the four different Standards+Innovation categories. Get to know all the nominees for the 2026 Standards+Innovation Awards here. The Education award will be celebrated during the final event of the Edu4Standards.eu project in Brussels on 25 November. All members and other interested parties are invited to the event upon prior registration on the event page. The time and place of the award ceremony for the other three awards will be announced later. TAGS: Standards+Innovation

item.title: Celebrating the European Week of Sport with standards
item.description: Every year, the European Week of Sport takes place from 23 to 30 September, encouraging people across Europe to embrace a more active lifestyle. This year’s campaign highlights that physical activity can take many forms and should fit each person’s circumstances. Whether you walk, cycle, run, swim or simply play, standards help make physical activity safer and more enjoyable. Even during a simple walk outside, you can discover that standards are everywhere. EN 13201-2:2015 sets performance requirements for road lighting, helping pedestrians see and be seen in urban areas, which is especially important during the darker months. item.title: CEPS Report Highlights the Role of Standardization in FP10 and the European Competitiveness Fund
item.description: CEN and CENELEC are pleased to share the report from the joint CEPS event, "From Research to Market: Standardization in FP10 and the European Competitiveness Fund (ECF)", held in Brussels on 10 September 2026. The event brought together policymakers, researchers, industry representatives, SMEs and standardization experts to discuss how standardization can strengthen the impact of European research and innovation and support Europe's competitiveness. More than 100 participants attended the event. Discussions highlighted the importance of integrating standardization more systematically into future EU funding programmes. item.title: Launch of the CEN Workshop 'Guidance for refuelling and bunkering of ammonia fuelled maritime and inland waterway vessels'
item.description: A new CEN Workshop is being established to provide much-needed guidance for ammonia refuelling points and bunkering for ammonia fuelled vessels. The project’s vision is to capture industry best practices for the safe use and storage of ammonia as a marine fuel. Bunkering is a vital process for the shipping industry as it ensures that marine vessels have sufficient fuel available to be able to complete their journeys. Traditionally, marine fuels have included petroleum-based residual and distillate oils. However, more recently, alternative “green” fuels such as ammonia are being used. Ammonia is an important substitute as it contributes to maritime decarbonisation and is in line with the EU’s Alternative Fuels Infrastructure (AFI) activities. item.title: New Edition of EN ISO 9001: Supporting Quality Management in a Changing World
item.description: CEN is happy to announce that it has published a new edition of EN ISO 9001 ‘Quality Management Systems – Requirements’ in parallel with ISO. As the European adoption of the world’s most widely used quality management standard, EN ISO 9001:2026 supports organizations in applying a common, internationally recognized framework for quality management across Europe. For almost four decades, EN ISO 9001 has helped organizations of all sizes and sectors build trust, improve consistency, and deliver products and services that meet customers’ and regulatory requirements. The 2026 revision updates this framework to reflect today's business realities, including faster technological developments, increasingly complex market conditions, and evolving stakeholder expectations. item.title: A new CEN Workshop Agreement to support AI skills and professionalism
item.description: Artificial Intelligence is transforming the way we work, learn, and innovate. At the same time, its rapid development raises important questions about the skills and ethical foundations needed to use AI effectively and responsibly. A key part of this discussion concerns how people are educated and trained to become AI literate. While more highly skilled AI professionals are entering the labour market, Europe still faces a shortage of ICT specialists with the skills needed to develop, deploy and use AI systems responsibly. To support these efforts, CEN has just published the Workshop Agreement CWA 18398 ‘AI Professional Role Profiles and Educational Profiles’. item.title: New Technical Specification Supports the Transition to a Circular Textile Economy
item.description: The recently published CEN/TS 18272-1 ‘Textiles – Circular economy for textile products – Part 1: General principles and guidance’ provides a common European framework for applying circular economy principles to textile products and the textile value chain. It brings together key principles, terminology and guidance, helping stakeholders develop a shared understanding of circularity in the textile sector. This Technical Specification covers topics such as the relationship between textiles and the circular economy, circular strategies, technical and biological cycles, terminology, and the role of material choices throughout the life cycle of textile products.
